I indicated this morning that I intended to reserve my ruling on the request of the Hon. Member for Westmorland-Kent (Mr. Robichaud) to hold an emergency debate under Standing Order 29. The matter raised by the Hon. Member is certainly very important. However, the conditions set down in Standing Order 29 are quite strict. While the situation in Moncton is serious, I have to refuse this request because it does not meet the criteria established under Standing Order 29. I would like to say to the Hon. Member that the refusal to accept an application for an emergency debate must in no way be taken as an indication from the Chair that the matter is not in itself very important. I want all Hon. Members to understand that and I thank the Hon. Member for raising the matter.

those persons employed on a commission basis in the area of sales. Sales commissions and expenses should also be considered in the same manner as wages. Salesmen who were on the road and incurred expenses can be left high and dry under the current law. Once again I urge the Minister to reconsider changing the Bankruptcy Act and to ensure that suppliers of goods, wage-earners, and sales people on commission receive priority treatment ahead of secured creditors such as banks, Crown corporations, Crown agencies, Revenue Canada, sales tax departments, and so on. It is long overdue. These people should get what is rightfully theirs. Again I commend the Minister on his initiative, but I also say to him that it is time to redress a grave injustice to many Canadians.
